data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003's counterexample assumes that 'the large service has internalized and diversified' the bottleneck (e.g., DNS/CA/routing), but the problem fixes the large service as having strictly more total internal redundancy, not strictly more diversity of every critical subsystem. Internalizing a dependency does not entail diversifying it; a large service can internalize its own CA or routing hub and still have a single internal point of failure. So the counterexample does not demonstrate that decentralization is strictly less resilient — it only shows that some decentralized deployments with hidden hubs can be brittle. Against a large service that merely has more redundant copies of the same internalized hub, the bottleneck counterexample collapses to a tie, not a strict win for the large service. The target overstates the counterexample by confounding internalization with genuine diversification.
